meta.title: Seasons Around the World — Set 1
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Comprehension quiz for 'Seasons Around the World' — global seasonal differences.

questions.question: How are the days in winter compared to other seasons?
options: They are longer than other seasons.
They are shorter than other seasons.
questions.explanation: During winter, the days are shorter than they are during other seasons, meaning we have less daylight.

questions.question: In some parts of the world, there are only two seasons: a rainy season and a dry season.
questions.explanation: True. Some tropical regions do not have four seasons; they only have wet (rainy) and dry seasons.

questions.question: When it is winter in the northern part of the world, what season is it in the southern part?
questions.explanation: The northern and southern halves of the Earth have opposite seasons. When the north has winter, the south has summer.

questions.question: Near the North Pole, the sun shines bright all day during winter.
questions.explanation: False. Near the North Pole, the sun never shines in winter, making it dark all day.

questions.question: What helps plants grow in the summer?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The sunlight helps plants grow in the summer.'

questions.question: The seasons do not change much near the _______, which is the imaginary middle line of Earth.
questions.hint: The warm line around the middle of the Earth.
questions.explanation: Seasons near the equator stay very similar all year long. Spring is like all other seasons there.

questions.question: In summer, the sun never sets in which coldest place on Earth?
questions.explanation: The text says: 'In summer, the sun never sets in Antarctica!' It stays light all day and night.

questions.question: Sort these facts from the story into Winter facts or Summer facts:
items: The sun never sets in Antarctica
People spend time in the sun

categories.label: Summer Facts
answers: The sun never sets in Antarctica
People spend time in the sun

questions.explanation: Wintry days have short daylight, plant sleep, and animal hibernation. Summer has non-setting sun in Antarctica and people playing outside.

questions.question: Some butterflies travel from the United States to Mexico in the fall to stay warm in winter.
questions.explanation: True. The text says butterflies travel to Mexico in the fall so they can stay warm.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show when spring comes:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Spring comes after winter.' This is the order of the seasons.

questions.question: What happens to leaves on some trees during fall?
options: They turn green and grow buds.
They change colors and drop to the ground.
They grow thick coats of fur.
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The leaves on some trees change colors and drop to the ground' during fall.

questions.question: In spring, baby animals are _______.
questions.explanation: The text says: 'In many places, baby animals are born' in spring.

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe Antarctica in summer:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'In summer the sun never sets in Antarctica.' This is due to Earth's tilt.

questions.question: Near the equator, spring is very different from winter and summer.
questions.explanation: False. Near the equator, seasons don't change much. Spring is like all the other seasons.

questions.question: How do animals prepare for winter in the fall?
options: They go swimming to stay cool.
They eat a lot and some store food.
They fly to the North Pole.
They stop growing and some die.
questions.explanation: In fall, animals get ready for winter by eating a lot and storing food so they have enough during the cold months.
